gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-roboto-serif: Roboto Serif spreads its letters out, with wide-open eyes on every e and a and a faint thick-and-thin pressure like worn charcoal. Aaargh, by comparison, draws bowls and stems at the same line width, so the display heading feels cut from a single stroke.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-sedan: Aaargh looks like glass tubing bent into letters, every bowl and stem the same width, with a generous opening into each e. Sedan's mellow, bookish strokes give it the quieter side of the bargain.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-trykker:
Aaargh has the look of steel cable bent into letters.

Trykker, with its gently tilted nib-like verticals and open counters, would carry a long passage with a literary, unhurried ease.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-plein: Alien Encounters stretches its tall lowercase across wide gaps between letter pairs, giving the heading an otherworldly, technological look. Plein stays reliable, with clear channels into every round letter.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-roundo: Otherworldly spacing and a high x-height define Alien Encounters, while Roundo keeps its lowercase n tidy, with arch and stem matching. And its small counters never clog, which gives the heading plenty of room to be strange.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings in every curve. Next to it, Alien Encounters feels almost like a signal from elsewhere, with its wide gaps and towering lowercase.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Amadeus runs wide across the line, its rounded-nib strokes ending without any swelling, and nothing tilts its round letters. Noto Rashi Hebrew follows like lightly engraved brass, bookish and gently modulated.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-devanag: Noto Serif Devanagari keeps short ascenders over a big lowercase body, with curves that thin slightly at the tops of round letters. Amadeus, by contrast, draws wirelike strokes of one thickness.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Amadeus draws its strokes like thread stitched along a path, stretching words wide with gaps between curve ends and stems. Noto Serif Dogra brings sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones, a bookish texture like crayon on rough paper.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-ethiopi: Amadeus stretches its words wide, with joins as thick as its strokes and no tilt in the round letters. Noto Serif Ethiopic settles words into solid blocks with soft, modest modulation, so the heading's boldness has something bookish to lean on.
